CLM-MAT-0218.statement: The THz amplitude of the ZnO/Ni/Pt heterostructure is increased by up to approximately 2.8 times compared with the Ni/Pt reference.

evidence_spans: In contrast, the ZnO/Ni/Pt trilayer shows a much stronger THz response, with  amplitude approximately 2.5 times larger than that of the Ni/Pt bilayer.
THz emission spectroscopy measurements were performed at room temperature in a dry air environment with relative humidity below 5%.
CLM-MAT-0219.statement: The THz time-domain signal amplitude of ZnO(40 nm)/Ni(3 nm)/Pt(3 nm) is approximately 2.5 times larger than that of the Ni(3 nm)/Pt(3 nm) bilayer.

extra_quotes: Bilayer and trilayer samples were deposited on 1 -mm-thick glass substrates by magnetron sputtering at room temperature.
THz emission spectroscopy measurements were performed at room temperature in a dry air environment with relative humidity below 5%.
Femtosecond laser pulses were incident normal to the sample surface from the substrate side.

ZnO/Fe/Pt does not exhibit a comparable enhancement relative to Fe/Pt , as confirmed by the other measurements shown in Fig. S11 of Supplemental Materials. This behavior is quite different from the strong enhancement observed in ZnO/Ni/Pt, indicating that the oxide-interface-induced enhancement is most effective for Ni/Pt.
In addition, the absence of enhancement when Ni was replaced by Co also highlights the uniqueness of Ni/ZnO interface, instead of a generic effect existent for all ZnO/FM systems
